overview: Middle school teachers work with students in grades 6 to 8, a time of big changes for young teens. They prepare classrooms and materials, teach one or more subjects, observe each student's progress and behavior, and work with parents and counselors. O*NET rates learning strategies at 4.25 out of 5 for this job and speaking at 4.12. Public schools require a bachelor's degree and a state license, and 21% report a post-baccalaureate certificate in O*NET data. The BLS May 2025 median is $64,370 across 620,090 jobs. Days are on your feet, and grading often stretches the week.
pay: Middle school teachers earn a median of $64,370, and the top 10% earn $102,540 or more. Washington pays the most at $102,140, 59% above the national figure, ahead of California at $98,950. Texas employs the most, 80,160, at a median of $63,390. Mississippi and Oklahoma pay the least.

faq.q: How much do middle school teachers make?
faq.a: The BLS May 2025 median is $64,370 a year. The middle half earn between $58,530 and $80,490. Washington, California and New York ($94,840) pay the most, while Mississippi ($50,790) and Oklahoma ($48,440) have the lowest state medians. Pay rises with experience and graduate credits.

faq.q: What degree do you need to teach middle school?
faq.a: Public schools require a bachelor's degree and a state teaching license. In O*NET data, 67% of middle school teachers hold a bachelor's degree and 21% a post-baccalaureate certificate, often a teaching credential. There are 12 related majors, including middle school education.

It can be. In O*NET data the job ranks above 91% of U.S. jobs for working more than 40 hours a week, and you spend long hours on your feet. Self-control and cooperation stand out as work styles, since young teens need patience and structure.

faq.q: What can middle school teachers do instead?
faq.a: Adult education and ESL instructors are a 94% match. Instructional Coordinators are a 79% match and earn $77,440, 20% more, according to BLS May 2025 data. Postsecondary English teachers are an 80% match and earn $78,760, 22% more, but usually need a graduate degree.
